selectedCourseReview.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly teaches practical criticism, fiction, poetry, drama and narrative form, supplying the literary-analysis foundation

selectedCourseReview.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly teaches argument, rhetorical theory and persuasive writing/speaking, contributing to the target communication strand without implying English-proficiency instruction

selectedCourseReview.name: Modern History
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary modern historical study of industrialisation, sovereignty, war, welfare and decolonisation needed to interpret nineteenth-/twentieth-century cultural works; it is not British history alone

selectedCourseReview.name: Great Literary Works
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies literary genres, primary texts and their historical themes across Western literary heritage; it is not a dedicated survey of British or American periods

selectedCourseReview.name: Style & Meaning
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly analyses linguistic choices and interpretive effects in literary and non-fiction texts through stylistics; it does not supply an English phonology or syntax sequence

selectedCourseReview.name: Histories of Gender
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies American gender histories through storybooks, interviews, queer cinema and cultural storytelling, contributing a defined cultural-history strand

selectedCourseReview.name: Rhetoric in Action
selectedCourseReview.contribution: applies public-speaking, debating and storytelling pedagogy with primary-school children after rhetorical foundations; interaction is principally Dutch, and this is neither secondary-school English teaching nor an English-proficiency course

selectedCourseReview.name: World Myth & Literature
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary comparative study of myth transmission, oral narrative and text-to-image transformations across cultures; it situates English-language literary study within global narrative traditions without claiming English-specific coverage

selectedCourseReview.name: Introduction to Film & Media
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly develops film-form and representation analysis to study narratives as cultural production and responses to social change

selectedCourseReview.name: Media Archaeology
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary study of printed books and pre-digital media as material objects shaping the circulation of knowledge, communication and cultural memory

selectedCourseReview.name: Introduction to Sociology
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary theories of race, gender, class and institutions for analysing social relations represented in literature and media

selectedCourseReview.name: Life & Travel Writing
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies memoir, autobiography, travel writing and cultural self-representation, including memory and identity in life narratives

selectedCourseReview.name: From T.V. to TikTok
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly examines American mainstream media and everyday life from television to TikTok, including storytelling, identity and whose accounts are heard

selectedCourseReview.name: Native American Histories
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies Indigenous histories and cultural resistance within the United States through memoir, literature, music, language revival and film; it does not relabel Indigenous culture as English culture

selectedCourseReview.name: The Documentary
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly analyses documentary histories, genres and the ethical representation of people, with an essay and short documentary production

selectedCourseReview.name: Film & Text
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly analyses literary adaptation and film form, with documented British-text examples including Pride and Prejudice, Frankenstein and Hamlet; its scope remains wider than English Studies

selectedCourseReview.name: Media & Race
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies race, systemic oppression and cultural representation in American history from the nineteenth century onward, including research-based podcast production

selectedCourseReview.name: History of Empires
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary analysis of imperial power and its historical rise/fall for studying English-speaking cultural worlds; it does not teach the historical spread of English itself

selectedCourseReview.name: Modern Sociology
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary theories of modernity, imperialism and colonial responses for interpreting cultural narratives and power, rather than generic social breadth

selectedCourseReview.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly applies feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic approaches in a literary research project

selectedCourseReview.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly studies and practices poetic form, voice, rhythm and performance through critical reading and creative projects

selectedCourseReview.name: History Research Seminar
selectedCourseReview.contribution: directly investigates the 1809 British Walcheren expedition through diaries, memoirs and official reports, providing a documented British historical subject and primary-source research

selectedCourseReview.name: Philosophy of Emotion
selectedCourseReview.contribution: provides specific complementary analysis of emotions toward fiction and art and the relationship between aesthetic and moral emotion; this is one interpretive contribution, not the whole programme
